problem.title: Retail demand forecasting
problem.context: A three-person data science team forecasts weekly demand for 400 stores and 30,000 products over an eight-week horizon. Nightly sales data and promotion and holiday effects feed Monday replenishment. The central data warehouse is outside the team's control.

requirements.text: Produce, every week, the forecast per store and product for the next eight weeks, and deliver it to the replenishment system by Monday 06:00.
Run the forecast again for any past week exactly as it was produced.
Try new model ideas and compare them with the production model on past weeks before they replace it.
Asked for the forecast of a week up to two years back, the team produces the same numbers within one working day.
A new model idea that beats the production model on past weeks reaches production within one week, with no manual step except the approval.
When a weekly run fails, the team is told within 15 minutes, and the replenishment system never receives a partial forecast.
A new team member can run the whole pipeline on their own machine within their first week.
Three data scientists, with no data engineers; the data warehouse stays as it is.
The weekly run must fit in the six hours between the nightly load and the Monday deadline.

approaches.idea: What if a managed batch service owns routine execution and operations while the team keeps the modeling workflow portable?
What if forecasting stays close to the warehouse to minimize data movement and infrastructure?
What if a managed ML platform owns experimentation and model promotion?
What if one containerized workflow runs locally and in cloud batch for portability?
What if warehouse compute is retained but input history and release controls are made reproducible and safe?
approaches.dropped_because: Frozen extracts and managed release controls do not resolve uncertain warehouse compute capacity within the six-hour deadline.

adrs.title: Where should forecast computation run?
adrs.context: The workload must finish by Monday 06:00 and a small team cannot maintain complex infrastructure. Managed operations, portability and modeling features have different costs.

adrs.context: Historical forecasts must reproduce their exact numbers despite changing source tables. Model code alone is not enough.
